approach.title: A clear method on every engagement
approach.description: The same three steps apply whether we advise on a single decision or run a programme for years.

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: We start with your objectives, constraints and risks, and agree what success looks like in numbers.

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: We turn objectives into a schedule, a budget and a responsibility map that every party can read.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.text: We stay on site and in the data, reporting early on variances so decisions are made while they are cheap.

services.metaDescription: Project management, engineering review, feasibility advisory and logistics planning from Arvand Partners.
services.title: Services
services.description: Four connected disciplines that cover a project from the investment decision to the last delivery.

process.title: How an engagement runs
process.description: Every service follows the same simple rhythm.

steps.title: Scope
steps.text: A short paid study to define the question, the data we need and the decision you must make.

steps.title: Work
steps.text: A named lead and a small team work inside your process, with a weekly written update.

steps.title: Hand over
steps.text: You keep the models, templates and training, so the result does not depend on us.

project-management.title: Project management and controls
project-management.summary: Owner-side management, scheduling and cost control for large programmes.
project-management.intro: We act as your representative on large projects: setting up the schedule and budget baseline, coordinating contractors and reporting honestly on progress and risk.
deliverables: Risk register with owners and mitigation dates
project-management.outcome: Fewer surprises. Typical clients see delays flagged six to eight weeks earlier than before.

engineering-review.title: Engineering design review
engineering-review.summary: Independent review of designs, specifications and constructability.
engineering-review.intro: A second pair of experienced eyes before you commit to construction. We review drawings, specifications and bills of quantities for errors, omissions and avoidable cost.
deliverables: Design review report with ranked findings
Value engineering options with cost impact
engineering-review.outcome: Problems found on paper, where fixing them costs a fraction of fixing them on site.

feasibility-advisory.title: Feasibility and investment advisory
feasibility-advisory.summary: Market, technical and financial studies that support a clear go or no-go.
feasibility-advisory.intro: Before capital is committed we test the idea against demand, site conditions, regulation and returns, and we say plainly when a project should not proceed.
feasibility-advisory.outcome: A decision you can defend to partners, lenders and your own board.

logistics-planning.title: Supply chain and logistics planning
logistics-planning.summary: Cross-border freight, site logistics and warehouse planning.
logistics-planning.intro: We design the flows of materials and goods that keep projects and operations moving across borders, ports and customs regimes.
deliverables: Route and mode analysis across Türkiye and the Gulf
logistics-planning.outcome: Materials arrive when the site needs them, not a month before or after.

marmara-logistics-hub.title: Marmara Logistics Hub
marmara-logistics-hub.summary: A 120,000 m² distribution centre planned around rail and port access.
marmara-logistics-hub.challenge: The developer had a fixed opening date tied to an anchor tenant, but the site layout and the freight flows had been designed separately.
marmara-logistics-hub.approach: We merged both into one model, resequenced the earthworks and moved the truck marshalling area, which removed a conflict with the rail spur.
marmara-logistics-hub.result: The hub opened on the agreed date. Truck turnaround in the first quarter was 22 percent faster than the tenant's target.

levant-office-campus.title: Levant Office Campus
levant-office-campus.summary: A five-building office campus delivered in two phases.
levant-office-campus.challenge: Design changes during tendering had pushed the budget 14 percent above the approved figure.
levant-office-campus.approach: A design review and value engineering workshop identified savings in the facade and mechanical systems without reducing floor area.
levant-office-campus.result: Budget returned to within 2 percent of the original figure and phase one finished three weeks early.

harbor-terminal-expansion.title: Harbor Terminal Expansion
harbor-terminal-expansion.summary: Berth and yard expansion while the terminal stayed in operation.
harbor-terminal-expansion.challenge: Construction had to happen beside live container operations with no loss of throughput.
harbor-terminal-expansion.approach: We built a phased work plan around vessel schedules and a daily coordination meeting between the contractor and the terminal operator.
harbor-terminal-expansion.result: Zero lost vessel calls during construction and the new berth entered service on schedule.

city-centre-tower.title: City Centre Tower
city-centre-tower.summary: A 42-storey mixed-use tower with a tight urban site.
city-centre-tower.challenge: The investor needed to know whether the mix of offices and serviced apartments would earn the required return.
city-centre-tower.approach: A feasibility study compared four programmes with demand data and a sensitivity model, then we managed the selected scheme.
city-centre-tower.result: The recommended mix raised projected yield by 1.8 points and the tower was topped out in 29 months.

riverside-residences.title: Riverside Residences
riverside-residences.summary: A low-rise residential development on a river plot.
riverside-residences.challenge: Flood risk and soil conditions were not fully reflected in the foundation design.
riverside-residences.approach: We reviewed the geotechnical report and drainage design and proposed a revised foundation and levels strategy.
riverside-residences.result: The revised design avoided a planned redesign during construction and saved an estimated four months.

steelworks-modernization.title: Steelworks Modernization
steelworks-modernization.summary: Replacement of a rolling line during planned shutdowns.
steelworks-modernization.challenge: Long-lead equipment from three countries had to arrive in a shutdown window of only nine weeks.
steelworks-modernization.approach: We mapped lead times, secured transport slots early and rehearsed the installation sequence with the plant team.
steelworks-modernization.result: The line restarted within the window and ramped to full output two weeks ahead of plan.

about.metaDescription: The story, values and history of Arvand Partners, a fictional engineering and project consultancy.
about.title: Independent advice from people who have built things
about.description: Arvand Partners is a consultancy of engineers, planners and logistics specialists.

story.title: Our story
story.imageAlt: An empty boardroom with a long table and city views
paragraphs: Arvand Partners began in 2008 as a three-person engineering review practice in Istanbul. Clients kept asking us for the next step: not only to find the problem, but to help fix it.

Today we are a team of specialists in two offices, working with owners, developers and operators across Türkiye and the Middle East. We do not build and we do not sell materials, so our advice stays independent.
We take the name from the river that links regions: a reminder that projects succeed when the people and flows around them are connected.

items.title: Independence
items.text: We have no stake in the contractor or supplier you choose. We work only for the client.

items.title: Plain reporting
items.text: Short, honest reports that say what is late, why, and what to decide.

items.title: Knowledge that stays
items.text: We leave you the models, templates and training, not a dependency.
Founded in Istanbul as an engineering review practice.
Project management and controls service launched.
Dubai office opened to serve Gulf clients.
Logistics and supply chain planning joined the firm.
Passed 140 delivered projects in nine countries.

items.question: Do you work outside Türkiye and the Gulf?
items.answer: Yes. Most work is in Türkiye and the Middle East, but we take projects in neighbouring regions when we can staff them well.

items.question: How do engagements start?
items.answer: With a short paid scoping study. It defines the question and the plan, and you can stop there if it is not right.

items.question: Do you also build or supply materials?
items.answer: No. We stay independent so our advice is never tied to a contractor or supplier.
